cues: The plant’s enormous paddle-shaped leaves split into ribbons along their parallel veins after strong winds.
A soft central stem is wrapped in overlapping leaf bases, creating a trunklike column rather than woody bark.
Its flower bud hangs downward, with purple bracts enclosing rows of developing fruitlets.
Most cultivated varieties contain only tiny undeveloped seeds embedded in their creamy pulp.
The plant’s underground corm sends up new shoots around the parent, forming dense connected clumps.
After flowering, the leafy stem dies back, while underground growth produces replacement shoots.
